title: Right adjoint commutes with direct sums
statement: Let f:X\to Y be a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] morphism of Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme] that is perfect, meaning of finite Tor dimension: for every x\in X the local ring \mathcal O_{X,x} has finite Tor dimension as an \mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}-module (for a morphism of finite type between Noetherian schemes this is the Stacks notion of a perfect morphism, under which \mathcal O_X is locally perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex] relative to Y), and let c be a right adjoint to the derived direct image Rf_* [def-pc-derived-direct-image] on the quasi-coherent derived categories D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) and D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y) [def-pc-derived-category]. Then c commutes with all set-indexed direct sums: for every family (K_j) in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y) the canonical map \bigoplus_j c(K_j)\to c(\bigoplus_j K_j) is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Let P be a perfect object on X. By the perfect-direct-image statement, Rf_*P is perfect on Y, and therefore it is compact in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y) by the perfect-compactness statement (Y is Noetherian, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated). Hence for every family (K_j) in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y) the canonical map \bigoplus_j \operatorname{Hom}(Rf_*P,K_j)\to\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_*P,\bigoplus_j K_j) is an isomorphism.

Adjunction identifies \operatorname{Hom}(P,c(\bigoplus_j K_j)) with \operatorname{Hom}(Rf_*P,\bigoplus_j K_j), and each \operatorname{Hom}(Rf_*P,K_j) with \operatorname{Hom}(P,c(K_j)); by compactness of P on X, \operatorname{Hom}(P,\bigoplus_j c(K_j))=\bigoplus_j\operatorname{Hom}(P,c(K_j)). Under these identifications, the map induced by the canonical morphism \bigoplus_j c(K_j)\to c(\bigoplus_j K_j) is the direct-sum isomorphism from step 1, so \operatorname{Hom}(P,-) of it is an isomorphism for every perfect P.

Fix the family (K_j) and let u:\bigoplus_j c(K_j)\to c(\bigoplus_j K_j) be the canonical map, with cone C in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X). By step 2, \operatorname{Hom}(P,u) is an isomorphism for every perfect P on X; since every shift P[n] is again perfect, the long exact Hom sequence of the triangle gives \operatorname{Hom}(P[n],C)=0 for all n\in\mathbb Z. The class of objects A with \operatorname{Hom}(A[n],C)=0 for all n\in\mathbb Z is closed under shifts, cones (long exact sequence), retracts, and arbitrary direct sums (\operatorname{Hom}(\bigoplus_i A_i,C)=\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,C)). It contains every perfect complex, so perfect generation implies it is all of D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X). Taking A=C gives \operatorname{id}_C=0, so C=0 and u is an isomorphism. Since the family was arbitrary, c commutes with all set-indexed direct sums.
